spec_match.rationale: Driving column-rule/row-rule longhands on a grid and transitioning them is the right surface, but the animation claim (the page's whole angle) is only declared via a transition — nothing demonstrates or verifies interpolation, and @keyframes animation is absent.

interactive.rationale: Color pickers, width sliders, style selects and five presets all restyle the live grid and regenerate the CSS output.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises slider-driven animated separators with presets, which is what the page implements.

edge_cases.rationale: No capability detection: in this browser (row-rule unsupported, conformance 2/6 fail) the grid renders with no rules at all while the lede claims smooth animation — a silent blank-rules state with no requires-Chrome-139+/flag notice; the 'none' style preset is the only edge covered.

references.rationale: No chromestatus.com/feature/5157805733183488 link on the page — see-also lists only sibling concepts, violating invariant 3.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers each longhand, both shorthands and a CSSOM round-trip, and honestly fails 6 of 8 in this browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified via headless Chromium 141 cloud fallback (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): controls and code output render, grid shows no rules (unsupported here), conformance panel 2/6/0; sliders/presets and the transition behaviour were not driven.

telemetry_health.rationale: Baseline injected telemetry only; no interaction events for the control panel.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout (code token colours via color-mix), preset buttons override background and color together on hover.

accessibility.rationale: Controls carry aria-labels and native semantics, but the .ctrl-label <label> elements are unassociated (no for/wrapping), aria-labels are terse ('Col Color'), and the generated CSS output has no live region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Grid and controls collapse at 600/540px and nothing is fixed-width; clean at 1280px headless but the ≈360px touch class was not exercised.

openQuestions.title: Add the missing ChromeStatus reference link
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3 requires chromestatus.com/feature/5157805733183488 on every page as the self-heal anchor; this page's see-also has only sibling links.

openQuestions.title: Detect missing gap-decoration support instead of rendering an empty stage
openQuestions.detail: In a browser without row-rule support (this Chromium 141 session) the grid shows plain gaps and every control appears to do nothing — no notice, no fallback. Probe CSS.supports('row-rule-color','red') (the suite's own assertion) and show the standard requires/flag banner when absent, keeping the controls live for the code output.

openQuestions.title: Actually demonstrate animation, not just a declared transition
openQuestions.detail: The page's distinct angle is that rules are animatable, but it only sets a transition and relies on the user noticing easing while dragging. Add an explicit 'Play animation' control (@keyframes cycling rule colour/width, honouring prefers-reduced-motion) and, ideally, read back interpolated getComputedStyle values mid-transition so the claim is observable — and verify against the spec whether rule properties interpolate or are discrete.

openQuestions.title: Associate the control labels and announce output changes
openQuestions.detail: Bind each .ctrl-label to its control with for/id (replacing the terse aria-labels), and give the generated CSS block an aria-live=polite or a copy button so non-visual users get the output.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/css-gap-decorations/animated-rules/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; in-page panel 2 pass / 6 fail / 0 blocked — row-rule and the shorthands are genuinely unsupported in this browser). The control panel, presets and generated CSS all render cleanly, but the stage shows a grid with no rules and no explanation, the page lacks its ChromeStatus anchor, and the animation angle is asserted rather than demonstrated. Controls were not driven headless.
